text: Who are to be sole judges of fair and unfair play, and all disputes shall be determined by them, each at his own Wicket; but in a Catch, which the Umpire, at the Bowler’s Wicket, cannot see sufficiently to decide upon, he may apply to the other Umpire, whose opinion is conclusive.
text_norm: who are to be sole judges of fair and unfair play, and all disputes shall be determined by them, each at his own wicket; but in a catch, which the umpire, at the bowler's wicket, cannot see sufficiently to decide upon, he may apply to the other umpire, whose opinion is conclusive.

text: The Umpires, in all Matches, to pitch fair wickets, and the parties to toss for the choice of Innings.
text_norm: the umpires, in all matches, to pitch fair wickets, and the parties to toss for the choice of innings.

text: They shall allow two minutes for each man to come in, and fifteen minutes between each Innings : when the umpire shall call “play,” the party refusing to play, shall lose the match.
text_norm: they shall allow two minutes for each man to come in, and fifteen minutes between each innings : when the umpire shall call "play," the party refusing to play, shall lose the match.

text: They are not to order a player out, unless appealed to by the adversaries.
text_norm: they are not to order a player out, unless appealed to by the adversaries.

text: But if the bowler’s foot is not behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, when he delivers the ball, they must, unasked, call “no ball.”
text_norm: but if the bowler's foot is not behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, when he delivers the ball, they must, unasked, call "no ball."

text: If the striker runs a short notch, the umpire must call “no notch.”
text_norm: if the striker runs a short notch, the umpire must call "no notch."

text: The umpires are not to be changed during the match, but by the consent of both parties:
text_norm: the umpires are not to be changed during the match, but by the consent of both parties:

text: must weigh not less than five ounces and a half, nor more than five ounces and three quarters.

text: At the begining of each innings, either party may call for a new ball.

text: must not exceed four inches and one quarter in the widest part.
text_norm: must not exceed four inches and one quarter in the widest part.

text: must be twenty-seven inches out of the ground; the bails, eight inches in length.
text_norm: must be twenty-seven inches out of the ground; the bails, eight inches in length.

text: must be in a line with the stumps, three feet in length, with a returncrease.
text_norm: must be in a line with the stumps, three feet in length, with a returncrease.

text: must be four feet from the wicket, and parallel to it.
text_norm: must be four feet from the wicket, and parallel to it.

text: must be opposite to each other, at the distance of twenty-two yards; which shall be pitched within thirty yards of a centre, by the adversaries.
text_norm: must be opposite to each other, at the distance of twenty-two yards; which shall be pitched within thirty yards of a centre, by the adversaries.

text: It shall not be lawful for either party, during a match, without the consent of the other, to alter the Ground, by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating.
text_norm: it shall not be lawful for either party, during a match, without the consent of the other, to alter the ground, by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating.

text: shall deliver the ball with one foot behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, and shall bowl four balls before he change wickets, which he shall do but once in the same innings.
text_norm: shall deliver the ball with one foot behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, and shall bowl four balls before he change wickets, which he shall do but once in the same innings.

text: He may order the striker, at his wicket, to stand on which side of it he please.

text: If the bowler tosses the ball over the striker’s head, or bowls it so wide that the striker cannot play at it, the party that is in shall be allowed one notch, to be put down as a wide ball; and those balls not to be reckoned as any of the four balls.

text: If the bowler bowls a no ball, the striker may play at it, and be allowed all the runs he can get, and shall not be put out except by running out.
text_norm: if the bowler bowls a no ball, the striker may play at it, and be allowed all the runs he can get, and shall not be put out except by running out.

text: must be bowled underhand, and delivered with the hand below the elbow.

text: In the event of a change of bowling, no more than two balls to be allowed in practice.
text_norm: in the event of a change of bowling, no more than two balls to be allowed in practice.

text: The bowler who takes the two balls to be obliged to bowl four balls.
text_norm: the bowler who takes the two balls to be obliged to bowl four balls.

text: if the bail is bowled off, or the stump bowled out of the ground.— Or, if the ball, from a stroke over or under the bat, or upon his hand, (but not wrist,) held before it touches the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher.—Or, if in striking, or at any other time while the ball is in play, both his feet are over the popping-crease, and his wicket put down, except his bat is grounded within it.— Or, if in striking at the ball, he hits down his wicket.- Or, if under pretence of running a notch, or otherwise, either of the strikers prevent a ball from being caught, the striker of the ball is out.— Or, if the ball is struck up, and he wilfully strikes it again.— Or, if in running a notch, the wicket is struck down by a throw, or with the ball in hand, before his foot, hand, or bat, is grounded over the popping-crease; but if the bail is off, the stump must be struck out of the ground.— Or, if the striker touches or takes up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the other party.

text: If with his foot or leg he stops the ball, which the bowler, in the opinion of the umpire at the bowler's wicket, shall have pitched in a straight line to the wicket and would have hit it.
text_norm: if with his foot or leg he stops the ball, which the bowler, in the opinion of the umpire at the bowler's wicket, shall have pitched in a straight line to the wicket and would have hit it.

text: If the players have crossed each other, he that runs for the wicket which is put down, is out;—if they are not crossed, he that has left the wicket which is put down, is out.
text_norm: if the players have crossed each other, he that runs for the wicket which is put down, is out;-if they are not crossed, he that has left the wicket which is put down, is out.

text: When a ball is caught, no notch to be reckoned.
text_norm: when a ball is caught, no notch to be reckoned.

text: When a striker is run out, the notch they were running for is not to be reckoned.
text_norm: when a striker is run out, the notch they were running for is not to be reckoned.

text: If a lost ball is called, the striker shall be allowed six: but if more than six are run before lost ball is called, then the striker to have all they run.
text_norm: if a lost ball is called, the striker shall be allowed six: but if more than six are run before lost ball is called, then the striker to have all they run.

text: When the ball has been in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, it is considered as no longer in play; and the strikers need not keep within their ground till the umpires have called “play:” but if the player goes out of his ground with an intent to run, before the ball is delivered, the bowler may put him out.

text: If the striker is hurt, he may retire from his wicket, and have his innings any time in that innings.

text: If the striker is hurt, some other person may be allowed to stand out for him, but not go in.

text: If any player stops the ball with his hat, the ball is to be considered as dead, and the opposite party is to add five notches to their score; if any are run, they are to have five in all.
text_norm: if any player stops the ball with his hat, the ball is to be considered as dead, and the opposite party is to add five notches to their score; if any are run, they are to have five in all.

text: If the ball is struck up, the striker may guard his wicket either with his bat or body.

text: In single wicket matches, if the striker moves out of his ground to strike at the bail, he shall be allowed no notch for such stroke.

text: Bets; If the notches of one player are laid against another, the bets depend on the first innings, unless otherwise specified.

text: If the bets are made upon both innings, and one party beats the other in one innings, the notches in the first innings shall determine the bet; but if the other party goes in a second time, then the bet must be determined by the number on the score.
